clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A healthcare worker will be required to use a tight-fitting respirator for a workplace respiratory hazard. Which requirements must be addressed before the worker's initial required respirator use?

options.A: Medical evaluation, appropriate fit testing, and required respirator training.
options.B: Respirator distribution, annual program review, and post-exposure medical testing.
options.C: Fit testing, vaccination screening, and documentation of prior respiratory exposures.
options.D: Training, symptom screening after first use, and a fit test only if leakage is reported.

semantic_correction.rationale: OSHA requires a written respiratory protection program when respirator use is required. The program includes medical evaluations, fit testing for tight-fitting respirators, and training. OSHA specifically requires the medical evaluation before fit testing or required workplace respirator use, fit testing before initial use of a tight-fitting facepiece, and training before the employee is required to use a respirator in the workplace. Option A contains these required pre-use elements without adding unrelated or delayed requirements.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Before initial required use of a tight-fitting respirator, ensure medical evaluation, appropriate fit testing, and respirator training are completed in accordance with OSHA requirements.
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Current federal OSHA standard accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: 29 CFR 1910.134(c)(1)(ii)–(iii),(vii)–(viii); §1910.134(e)(1) — medical evaluation before fit testing or required use; §1910.134(f)(1)–(2) — fit testing before initial use of tight-fitting facepiece; §1910.134(k)(1)–(3) — training before required workplace use
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: For required tight-fitting respirator use, OSHA requires medical evaluation, fit testing, and training; medical evaluation precedes fit testing or required use, fit testing precedes initial use, and training is provided before required workplace use.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the repeated 'only' distractor pattern and rebuilt all options as parallel three-part program elements while preserving OSHA's exact pre-use medical-evaluation, fit-testing, and training requirements.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed pp. 24 and 26
audit_findings_append.finding: The original concept was correct but distractors were structurally weak. The revised item tests the required pre-use elements with comparable triads and preserves the regulation's exact timing qualifications without inventing a mandated order between fit testing and training.

option_audit.A: Correct. All three elements are required by OSHA before initial required use in the circumstances described.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Distribution and program review do not replace the worker-specific medical evaluation, fit test, and training prerequisites; post-exposure testing is not a routine pre-use requirement.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Vaccination screening and prior-exposure documentation are not the OSHA respiratory-protection prerequisites tested here.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Fit testing is required before initial use of a tight-fitting respirator rather than waiting for reported leakage.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone contains the OSHA-required worker-specific medical evaluation, tight-fitting respirator fit test, and training needed before initial required use.
cueing_check: All four choices are three-part program-element sets of comparable length and syntax; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.

checks: no unsupported fixed sequence between fit testing and training asserted
